newsitem.title: FRANCE: France deplores move to ease ivory trade ban.
newsitem.headline: France deplores move to ease ivory trade ban.

text.p: France's new leftist government on Thursday condemned a decision to allow three southern African states to conditionally sell ivory to Japan from their "excess" elephant herds.

"The vote which has just taken place is the signal for a resumption of ivory trafficking throughout Africa," Environment Minister Dominique Voynet, a member of the French Greens party, said in a statement.

Meeting in Harare, a world forum on endangered species known as the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) lifted a seven-year-old global ban in ivory trade and backed the "experimental" deal.
Seventy-six countries voted for the proposal and 21 against. There were 20 abstentions in the secret ballot on the proposal by Zimbabwe, Botswana and Namibia.

Voynet, part of the leftist government which took power in France earlier this month, said the ban on ivory trade had not yet been in effect long enough to allow the depleted elephant population to recover.
She said she regretted that, within the European Union, only France, Germany and Luxembourg had opposed the plan.
